What Is Programming?

Stage 1 Concept ⏱ 10 min 📖 Glossary

You already give instructions every day. Programming is writing them so clearly that even a very fast but very literal computer can follow them.

🔎 Motivating questionIf you had a robot helper that takes everything literally, how carefully would you word “make tea”?

Objectives

  • Explain programming in plain words
  • Tell instructions from data
  • Describe what a program does

Needs first: None — start here!

1 Start with an analogy

Real life first, code second.

A recipe card. Ingredients = data, steps = instructions, cook = computer. If a step is vague (“add some salt”), results vary wildly.

⚠️ Where the analogy breaksWhere it breaks: a human cook guesses. A computer never guesses — vague steps crash or do the wrong thing. Precision is the whole game.

2 The concept, plainly

One idea at a time, words before jargon.

A program is a list of exact instructions plus the data they work on. Your music app, bank app, and games are all programs.

Programs do three things: take input (taps, files, sensors), process it (calculate, decide, repeat), and produce output (screen, sound, files).

You write programs in a programming language — a small, strict language with no small talk. Java is one of the most used.

3 Watch it move: Recipe becomes program

Step at your pace. Text explains every move.

4 Live code demo

Small, correct Java 17 (LTS) code. Read, trace, copy.

Main.javaJava 17
// A program is input -> process -> output
// Input:  two numbers. Process: add. Output: sum.
int a = 4;
int b = 5;
int sum = a + b;        // process
System.out.println(sum); // output: 9
▶ Output 9
  • Lines 3-4 store data in named boxes.
  • Line 5 processes: adds them.
  • Line 6 outputs the result.
💡 Why this output?The computer did not “understand” adding like you do. It followed the + instruction on the two stored values and printed the result.

5 Interactive experiment

Change values, watch consequences. Simulation — honest, not a real compiler.

Try it (visual simulation — not a real compiler)
Change the numbers and operator — the computer just follows orders.
…

6 Common mistakes (at least 3)

Wrong, why, fixed — learn from realistic slips.

❌ Mistake 1: “The computer will figure out what I mean.”Why: Computers take everything literally. “Sort of 5” is meaningless to them.
✅ Fix: Say exactly what to do: add 5, print the result, stop.
❌ Mistake 2: Thinking data and instructions are the same.Why: Data (4, 5) sits still. Instructions (+, print) act on it.
✅ Fix: Label each line: is this storing, doing, or showing?
❌ Mistake 3: Starting with a huge app idea.Why: Big programs are hundreds of small instruction lists combined.
✅ Fix: Start with input → one step → output. Grow from there.

7 Guided practice

Hints first, solutions only after a real try.

Label the parts

Look at the code above. Write I (input/data), P (process), or O (output) next to each line.

HintLines with = store data. + processes. println shows.
Solutiona, b, sum declarations = data/input; a + b = process; println = output.
Write a 5-step recipe

Write exact steps for “brush teeth” as if for a literal robot. No step may assume guessing.

HintInclude amounts, order, and when to stop.
SolutionExample: 1 pick up brush, 2 add pea-size paste, 3 brush top teeth 30s, 4 brush bottom 30s, 5 rinse 5s, stop.

8 Lesson quiz

3+ questions. Attempts saved locally; review queue learns your weak spots.

9 Takeaways + next step

  • A program = exact instructions + data.
  • Input → process → output explains every app.
  • Computers never guess; precision is kindness to them.
  • Java is one language for writing such instructions.
🧠 Recall challengeSay in one sentence: what does a program do with input?
✏️ Do on your ownFind one app you used today and name its input, process, and output.
